clone.title: How Rc::clone works
clone.description: Makes another owner of the same value by counting references; nothing is copied.

title.text: let a = Rc::new(String::from("hi")); let b = Rc::clone(&a);

slides.caption: Rc puts the value on the heap together with a counter of how many owners it has.
a is the first owner: the count is 1.
Rc::clone(&a) gives a second pointer to the same String and increases the count.
When an owner goes out of scope the count goes down; at 0 the String is freed.
Write Rc::clone(&a) rather than a.clone() so readers see that only a counter changes. Rc is single-threaded; Arc is the thread-safe version.

strong_count.title: How Rc::strong_count works
strong_count.description: How many Rc owners share the value right now.

note.text: after one clone and one drop

slides.caption: strong_count reads the counter that Rc keeps next to the value.
After Rc::new: 1.
After Rc::clone: 2.
After dropping the clone: 1 again.
Mostly useful for learning and debugging; normal code rarely needs to look at the count.

try_unwrap.title: How Rc::try_unwrap works
try_unwrap.description: Takes the value out of an Rc, but only if it is the last owner.

note.text: a and a clone b exist

slides.caption: With other owners still around, taking the value out would leave them pointing at nothing, so it is refused.
While b also owns it (count 2): Err, and you get your Rc back.
After b is dropped (count 1): Ok, and you own the value directly.
Rc::into_inner is a variant that returns an Option.

downgrade.title: How Rc::downgrade works
downgrade.description: Makes a Weak pointer that does not keep the value alive.

slides.caption: A Weak points at the value but does not count as an owner.
The strong count stays 1.
The weak count becomes 1.
Used for back-pointers, like a child pointing to its parent, to avoid reference cycles that would never be freed.

upgrade.title: How Weak::upgrade works
upgrade.description: Turns a Weak back into an Rc, if the value still exists.

slides.caption: upgrade checks the strong count: if it is above zero, you get a new Rc.
While an Rc owner exists: Some(Rc(5)).
After the last owner is dropped, the value is gone: None.
Always handle None: a Weak can outlive the value.

make_mut.title: How Rc::make_mut works
make_mut.description: Gives &mut to the value, cloning it first if others share it (clone-on-write).

slides.caption: If a is the only owner, make_mut changes the value in place. Here b shares it, so a gets its own copy first.
b also points at [1], so the Vec is cloned for a.
a's copy gets 2; b still sees [1].
Cheap sharing until someone writes: a common trick for persistent data.

new.title: How Rc::new works
new.description: Puts a value on the heap with a reference count of 1.

slides.caption: Rc = reference counted. Clones share the same value; it is freed when the count reaches 0.
The Vec moves into a new heap block.
One owner so far.
Rc is for one thread; use Arc to share across threads.

ptr_eq.title: How Rc::ptr_eq works
ptr_eq.description: true if two Rcs point at the very same value, not just equal ones.

slides.caption: a == c compares the values; ptr_eq compares the addresses.
b is a clone of a: same allocation, true.
c holds an equal value in another allocation: false.
Useful in graphs to check whether two nodes are the same node.

get_mut.title: How Rc::get_mut works
get_mut.description: Gives &mut to the value only if this is the only owner.

slides.caption: With one owner, changing the value is safe. With several, it would surprise the others.
Only one Rc exists: Some.
After a clone, two exist: None.
make_mut clones the value instead of returning None.

weak_count.title: How Rc::weak_count works
weak_count.description: How many Weak pointers point at the value.

slides.caption: Each Rc::downgrade adds one Weak.
Two Weak pointers were made.
weak_count is 2; strong_count is still 1.
The value is freed when the strong count hits 0, even if Weaks remain.

into_inner.title: How Rc::into_inner works
into_inner.description: Takes the value out if this was the last owner; otherwise None.

note.text: the last one out gets the value

slides.caption: Each call gives up one owner. Only the last owner receives the value.
a is not the last owner: None (a is dropped).
b is now the only owner: Some("x").
Unlike try_unwrap, it never hands the Rc back, so no value is ever lost by accident.

unwrap_or_clone.title: How Rc::unwrap_or_clone works
unwrap_or_clone.description: Gets an owned value: moves it out if unique, clones it if shared.

slides.caption: You always get the value; a clone only happens when necessary.
Unique: no copy needed.
Shared: the value is cloned, the others keep theirs.
Arc::unwrap_or_clone works the same across threads.

new_cyclic.title: How Rc::new_cyclic works
new_cyclic.description: Creates a value that holds a Weak pointer to itself.

slides.caption: The closure receives the future Weak pointer before the value exists.
The Node stores a Weak to itself.
After creation, that Weak upgrades to the same Rc.
Used for trees where nodes need to hand out pointers to themselves.

weak-new.title: How Weak::new works
weak-new.description: An empty Weak that points at nothing yet.

slides.caption: Weak::new allocates nothing; upgrade always returns None.
There is no value behind it.
upgrade() is None.
Typical as the starting value of a parent pointer before it is set.

weak-strong_count.title: How Weak::strong_count works
weak-strong_count.description: How many Rc owners the value still has, seen from a Weak.

slides.caption: A Weak can check whether its value is still alive.
One Rc owns the value: 1.
The Rc was dropped: 0.
upgrade() is the usual way to both check and use the value.

from.title: How Rc::from works
from.description: Moves a value (a String, Vec, Box, …) into a new Rc.

slides.caption: From a Vec you get a shared slice; from a String a shared str.
The elements move into the Rc allocation.
Clones now share them.
Rc<str> is a cheap-to-clone, immutable string.

from_iter.title: How Rc::from_iter works
from_iter.description: Collects an iterator into a shared Rc<[T]>.

slides.caption: No separate Vec is needed in your code.
The items are collected.
They live in one Rc allocation.
Arc<[T]> works the same way.

downcast.title: How Rc<dyn Any>::downcast works
downcast.description: Gets the concrete type back from an Rc<dyn Any>.

slides.caption: Checked at run time.
The type matches.
Ok(Rc<&str>).
Arc has the same for Arc<dyn Any + Send + Sync>.
The value can never move, and clones share it.
The value goes into an Rc.
It is pinned.
Box::pin is the single-owner version.

as_ptr.title: How Rc::as_ptr works
as_ptr.description: A raw pointer to the shared value.

slides.caption: All clones point to the same allocation.
Both pointers are compared.
Equal: true.
Rc::ptr_eq does this comparison for you.

rc_weak-ptr_eq.title: How rc::Weak::ptr_eq works
rc_weak-ptr_eq.description: true if two Weak pointers point to the same allocation.

a0t.text: w1, w2 from the same Rc

slides.caption: Works even after the value is gone.
Same Rc: true.
Different Rc: false.
Useful for removing a specific observer from a list.

rc_weak-weak_count.title: How rc::Weak::weak_count works
rc_weak-weak_count.description: How many Weak pointers exist, seen from a Weak.

slides.caption: Counts all Weak pointers to the allocation.
Two Weaks exist.
weak_count is 2.
Returns 0 if no strong owner is left.

default.title: How Rc::default works
default.description: A new Rc holding the inner type's default value.

slides.caption: Allocates an Rc around T::default().
Default for the inner type.
Wrapped in an Rc.
Arc::default does the same across threads.

new_uninit.title: How Rc::new_uninit works
new_uninit.description: Allocates an Rc whose value will be written later.

title.text: let mut r = Rc::<u32>::new_uninit(); Rc::get_mut(&mut r).unwrap().write(5);

slides.caption: Avoids building a large value on the stack first.
Allocate empty space.
Write 5, then assume_init (unsafe).
Arc::new_uninit works the same.

into_raw.title: How Rc::into_raw works
into_raw.description: Turns an Rc into a raw pointer, keeping the reference count.

title.text: let p = Rc::into_raw(r); let r = unsafe { Rc::from_raw(p) };

slides.caption: The count is not decreased; from_raw must take it back.
Rc becomes a raw pointer.
from_raw restores it.
Forgetting from_raw leaks the value.

rc_weak-as_ptr.title: How rc::Weak::as_ptr works
rc_weak-as_ptr.description: A raw pointer to the value a Weak points at.

slides.caption: Does not check whether the value still exists.
Get both pointers.
Equal.
Do not read through it after the Rc is gone.

from_raw.title: How Rc::from_raw works
from_raw.description: Turns a pointer from Rc::into_raw back into an Rc (unsafe).

slides.caption: Each into_raw needs exactly one from_raw.
Rebuild.
Read 3.
Otherwise the value leaks.

increment_strong_count.title: How Rc::increment_strong_count works
increment_strong_count.description: Adds one owner through a raw pointer (unsafe).

slides.caption: Pair it with from_raw or decrement later.
Add an owner.
Count 2.
Used when C code holds extra references.

decrement_strong_count.title: How Rc::decrement_strong_count works
decrement_strong_count.description: Removes one owner through a raw pointer (unsafe).

slides.caption: Reaching 0 frees the value.
Remove an owner.
Count 1.
Must match an earlier increment or into_raw.

assume_init.title: How Rc<MaybeUninit<T>>::assume_init works
assume_init.description: Turns an initialised Rc<MaybeUninit<T>> into Rc<T> (unsafe).

slides.caption: The value must be written first.
Write.
Declare initialised.
Rc::new is the usual path.

new_zeroed.title: How Rc::new_zeroed works
new_zeroed.description: An Rc whose memory is zero-filled, as Rc<MaybeUninit<T>>.

slides.caption: Sound to assume_init for integers.
Allocate zeroed.
assume_init.
Avoids building the value on the stack.

new_uninit_slice.title: How Rc::new_uninit_slice works
new_uninit_slice.description: An Rc<[MaybeUninit<T>]> of n elements to fill later.

slides.caption: Fill while the Rc is still unique.
Write 7, 8.
assume_init.
Rc::from(vec) is the safe way.

new_zeroed_slice.title: How Rc::new_zeroed_slice works
new_zeroed_slice.description: An Rc slice of n zeroed elements.

slides.caption: assume_init is sound for integers.
Allocate zeroed.
assume_init.
Rc::from(vec![0; 3]) is safe.

rc_weak-into_raw.title: How rc::Weak::into_raw works
rc_weak-into_raw.description: Turns a Weak into a raw pointer, keeping the weak count.

note.text: hand a weak handle to C

slides.caption: from_raw must take it back.
Convert.
Rebuild and upgrade.
Like Rc::into_raw, for weak references.

rc_weak-from_raw.title: How rc::Weak::from_raw works
rc_weak-from_raw.description: Turns a pointer from Weak::into_raw back into a Weak (unsafe).

slides.caption: Each into_raw needs one from_raw.
Rebuild.
weak_count is 1.
Otherwise the weak count leaks.
